## Walking {#bass-walk}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Walking**. It is built up from 3 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

One note on every beat (four quarter notes in 4/4, three in 3/4, dotted quarters in 12/8): the root on beat 1 when the chord changes, chord tones and scale steps in between, and an approach note on beat 4 that leads into the next bar.

It belongs in *Swing* and *Jazz ballad*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Walking","opts":{"bassFeel":"walk"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Two-feel

Half notes on beats 1 and 3, root then fifth, with an occasional pickup into the next bar. The lighter feel a band often plays on the head before the bass starts to walk.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-two) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Chord tones (learning to walk)

The chord spelled out, one note on every beat: root, 3rd, 5th, 7th, the same in every bar. When a bar has two chords, each gets its root and one more note. A step between playing roots and walking.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-arp) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Walking, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Beat 1: the root. Beats 2 and 3: any two other chord tones or scale steps. Beat 4: a note one fret above or below the next bar's root. Start from the chord tones of the step before and change only beat 4, then free up beats 2 and 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Walking","opts":{"bassFeel":"walk"}},{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Walking","opts":{"bassFeel":"walk"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Walking","opts":{"bassFeel":"walk"}}]'></div>

### Step 7: In 3/4

The same pattern in a jazz waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Walking","opts":{"bassFeel":"walk"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same bass line in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Jazz ballad**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ballad" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Walking","opts":{"bassFeel":"walk"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves), [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two), [Chord tones (learning to walk)](bass.qmd#bass-arp).
- **Leads to:** [Boogaloo riff, walking at times](bass.qmd#bass-riffwalk): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Four to the bar](chords.qmd#chords-four) (comping rhythm), [Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)](drums.qmd#drums-quarters) (drum groove), [Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)](drums.qmd#drums-ridetime) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in swing:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto) (comping rhythm), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the Jazz group:** [Chord tones (learning to walk)](bass.qmd#bass-arp), [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two), [Boogaloo riff](bass.qmd#bass-riff), [Boogie-woogie](bass.qmd#bass-boogie), [Boogie-woogie octaves](bass.qmd#bass-boogie-oct), [Yancey figure](bass.qmd#bass-yancey), [Boogaloo riff, walking at times](bass.qmd#bass-riffwalk).

## Chord tones (learning to walk) {#bass-arp}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Chord tones (learning to walk)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The chord spelled out, one note on every beat: root, 3rd, 5th, 7th, the same in every bar. When a bar has two chords, each gets its root and one more note. A step between playing roots and walking.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad*, *Boogaloo* and *Boogie-woogie*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Roots on every beat

The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-roots) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Chord tones (learning to walk), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root, 3rd, 5th, 7th, one to a beat, the same shape every bar. On a minor seventh chord the 3rd is three frets above the root; on a dominant or major chord, four. Say the chord tones as you play them.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}},{"label":"Roots on every beat (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Two-feel**. ### The pattern

Half notes on beats 1 and 3, root then fifth, with an occasional pickup into the next bar. The lighter feel a band often plays on the head before the bass starts to walk.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad* and *Stride piano*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

## Boogaloo riff {#bass-riff}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Boogaloo riff**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A repeated straight-eighths figure: root on 1, root pushed on the and of 2, then a fifth and flat seventh on beat 4 leading back to the root. The kind of line under Watermelon Man. In 6/8 and 12/8 it becomes a shuffle: each beat played long-short, climbing root, 3rd, 5th, 6th.

It belongs in *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the boogaloo style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff","opts":{"bassFeel":"riff"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)

The root on beat 1, again on the and of 2 and on beat 3, the same rhythm as the kick drum. Every second bar ends with an eighth note that leads into the next chord.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-dotted) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Boogaloo riff, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A straight-eighths riff: root on 1, root again on the and of 2, then fifth and flat seventh on beat 4 climbing back to the root. The push on the and of 2 is the same one as the dotted line; the ending is new. Play every bar the same.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff","opts":{"bassFeel":"riff"}},{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff","opts":{"bassFeel":"riff"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|Bb7 C7|F7|Gm7 C7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff","opts":{"bassFeel":"riff"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass.qmd#bass-dotted).
- **Leads to:** [Boogaloo riff, walking at times](bass.qmd#bass-riffwalk): the patterns that use this one as a step.

## Boogie-woogie {#bass-boogie}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Boogie-woogie**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Eight swung eighth notes a bar walking up the chord and back down: root, 3rd, 5th, 6th, flat 7th, 6th, 5th, 3rd, the same every bar. It is the boogie-woogie pianist's left hand, played on the bass. A chord that arrives on beat 3 starts the walk again from its root.

It belongs in *Boogie-woogie* and *Jump blues*. Here it is in the boogie-woogie style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie","opts":{"bassFeel":"boogie"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on every beat

Start with something simpler. The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-roots) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Chord tones (learning to walk)

The chord spelled out, one note on every beat: root, 3rd, 5th, 7th, the same in every bar. When a bar has two chords, each gets its root and one more note. A step between playing roots and walking.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-arp) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Boogie-woogie, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Eight swung eighths a bar, up the chord and back down: root, 3rd, 5th, 6th, flat 7th, 6th, 5th, 3rd. Learn the shape on one chord until the hand knows it, then move it up a fourth for the IV chord and a fifth for the V. The shape stays the same; only the root changes. Lean on beats 1 and 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogie-woogie","opts":{"bassFeel":"boogie"}},{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

## Boogie-woogie octaves {#bass-boogie-oct}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Boogie-woogie octaves**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. [All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Rolling octaves: the root and the root an octave higher in swung eighths, low on every beat and high on every and, the same every bar. A chord that arrives on beat 3 starts again from its low root.

It belongs in *Boogie-woogie* and *Jump blues*. Here it is in the boogie-woogie style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-roots) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

## Yancey figure {#bass-yancey}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Yancey figure**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

After Jimmy Yancey's slow-blues left hand: root on 1, fifth on the and of 1, root on the and of 2, fifth on 3, root on 4. A lilting, habanera-like figure for a slow blues. A chord that arrives on beat 3 starts on its root.

It belongs in *Boogie-woogie*. Here it is in the boogie-woogie style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Yancey figure","opts":{"bassFeel":"yancey"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="58" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Tango (habanera)

The habanera rhythm: root held for a beat and a half, the fifth on the and of 2, then the root an octave up on 3 and the fifth on 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-tango) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="58" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tango"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Yancey figure, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Clap it first: 1, the and of 1, the and of 2, 3, 4. Then play root on 1, fifth on the and, root on the and of 2, fifth on 3, root on 4. Play it slowly and lazily, like a slow blues; the notes between the beats give the lilt, so do not rush them.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="58" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Yancey figure","opts":{"bassFeel":"yancey"}},{"label":"Tango (habanera) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tango"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 84 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|C7|F7|C7|G7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Yancey figure","opts":{"bassFeel":"yancey"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogie" data-chart="C7|F7 F#dim7|C7|G7 F7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Yancey figure","opts":{"bassFeel":"yancey"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves), [Tango (habanera)](bass.qmd#bass-tango).
- **Plays with, in boogie-woogie:** [Boogie-woogie right hand](chords.qmd#chords-boogie) (comping rhythm), [Blues shuffle](drums.qmd#drums-shuffle) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the Jazz group:** [Walking](bass.qmd#bass-walk), [Chord tones (learning to walk)](bass.qmd#bass-arp), [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two), [Boogaloo riff](bass.qmd#bass-riff), [Boogie-woogie](bass.qmd#bass-boogie), [Boogie-woogie octaves](bass.qmd#bass-boogie-oct), [Boogaloo riff, walking at times](bass.qmd#bass-riffwalk).

## Boogaloo riff, walking at times {#bass-riffwalk}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Boogaloo riff, walking at times**. It is built up from 3 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The boogaloo riff, but about half the four-bar phrases end with a bar of walking quarter notes that leads into the next phrase, and now and then two bars.

It belongs in *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the boogaloo style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff, walking at times","opts":{"bassFeel":"riffwalk"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Boogaloo riff

Start with something simpler. A repeated straight-eighths figure: root on 1, root pushed on the and of 2, then a fifth and flat seventh on beat 4 leading back to the root. The kind of line under Watermelon Man. In 6/8 and 12/8 it becomes a shuffle: each beat played long-short, climbing root, 3rd, 5th, 6th.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-riff) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff","opts":{"bassFeel":"riff"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Chord tones (learning to walk)

The chord spelled out, one note on every beat: root, 3rd, 5th, 7th, the same in every bar. When a bar has two chords, each gets its root and one more note. A step between playing roots and walking.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-arp) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Walking

One note on every beat (four quarter notes in 4/4, three in 3/4, dotted quarters in 12/8): the root on beat 1 when the chord changes, chord tones and scale steps in between, and an approach note on beat 4 that leads into the next bar.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-walk) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Walking","opts":{"bassFeel":"walk"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Boogaloo riff, walking at times, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Riff most of the time; at the end of some four-bar phrases, walk one bar of quarter notes into the next phrase. The skill is the switch: feel where the phrase ends and land on the next root exactly on 1.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff, walking at times","opts":{"bassFeel":"riffwalk"}},{"label":"Walking (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"walk"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff, walking at times","opts":{"bassFeel":"riffwalk"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|Bb7 C7|F7|Gm7 C7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boogaloo riff, walking at times","opts":{"bassFeel":"riffwalk"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Plays with, in boogaloo:** [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs) (comping rhythm), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove), [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) (conga part).

## So What: the bass call {#bass-sowhat}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **So What: the bass call**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The bass has the melody. A two-bar figure: the root, then eighth notes up the scale from the fifth (5, 6, 7, root, 9) and back through the seventh to the root on the next downbeat. Then it waits for the chords to answer. Pair it with the So What comping rhythm.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the bass call","opts":{"bassFeel":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Held roots (the bass voice)

Start with something simpler. The root of every chord, held until the next chord: the bass part of a four-part hymn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-held) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Two-feel

Half notes on beats 1 and 3, root then fifth, with an occasional pickup into the next bar. The lighter feel a band often plays on the head before the bass starts to walk.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-two) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: So What: the bass call, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The bass has the tune here. Root, then eighth notes up from the fifth (5, 6, 7, root, 9), back down through the seventh to the root. Then wait while the chords answer. Sing it before playing it.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the bass call","opts":{"bassFeel":"sowhat"}},{"label":"Two-feel (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Dm7|Ebm7|Ebm7|Dm7|Dm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the bass call","opts":{"bassFeel":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"So What: the bass call","opts":{"bassFeel":"sowhat"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Held roots (the bass voice)](bass.qmd#bass-held), [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [So What: the answer](chords.qmd#chords-sowhat) (comping rhythm).
- **Plays with, in swing:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto) (comping rhythm), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the From tunes group:** [Killer Joe: two-bar vamp](bass.qmd#bass-killerjoe), [Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-songfather), [Footprints: waltz ostinato](bass.qmd#bass-footprints), [All Blues: 6/8 vamp](bass.qmd#bass-allblues), [Chameleon: chromatic pickup](bass.qmd#bass-chameleon), [Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm](bass.qmd#bass-maiden), [Take Five: 3 + 2](bass.qmd#bass-takefive).

## Killer Joe: two-bar vamp {#bass-killerjoe}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Killer Joe: two-bar vamp**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar figure for two chords a whole step apart: the root held for two beats, then two quarter notes that climb into the next root from below (C, G, A into B flat; B flat, G, B into C).

It belongs in *Swing* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="C7|Bb7|C7|Bb7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Killer Joe: two-bar vamp","opts":{"bassFeel":"killerjoe"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="C7|Bb7|C7|Bb7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Two-feel

Half notes on beats 1 and 3, root then fifth, with an occasional pickup into the next bar. The lighter feel a band often plays on the head before the bass starts to walk.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-two) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="C7|Bb7|C7|Bb7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Killer Joe: two-bar vamp, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two chords a whole step apart, two bars each. Hold the root for two beats, then two quarter notes climbing into the next root from below. The same shape takes you down from C7 to B♭7 and back up.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="C7|Bb7|C7|Bb7" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Killer Joe: two-bar vamp","opts":{"bassFeel":"killerjoe"}},{"label":"Two-feel (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="C7|Bb7|C7|Bb7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Killer Joe: two-bar vamp","opts":{"bassFeel":"killerjoe"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Killer Joe: two-bar vamp","opts":{"bassFeel":"killerjoe"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same bass line in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Boogaloo**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Killer Joe: two-bar vamp","opts":{"bassFeel":"killerjoe"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves), [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two).
- **Plays with, in swing:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto) (comping rhythm), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the From tunes group:** [So What: the bass call](bass.qmd#bass-sowhat), [Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-songfather), [Footprints: waltz ostinato](bass.qmd#bass-footprints), [All Blues: 6/8 vamp](bass.qmd#bass-allblues), [Chameleon: chromatic pickup](bass.qmd#bass-chameleon), [Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm](bass.qmd#bass-maiden), [Take Five: 3 + 2](bass.qmd#bass-takefive).

## Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave {#bass-songfather}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The figure the tune opens with: the root for a beat and a half, the fifth on the and of 2, the octave on beat 3 held to the end of the bar. Steely Dan borrowed it for Rikki Don't Lose That Number.

It belongs in *Bossa nova*. Here it is in the bossa nova style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Fm7|Fm7|Eb7|Eb7|Db7|C7|Fm7|Fm7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"songfather"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Fm7|Fm7|Eb7|Eb7|Db7|C7|Fm7|Fm7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)

The root on beat 1, again on the and of 2 and on beat 3, the same rhythm as the kick drum. Every second bar ends with an eighth note that leads into the next chord.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-dotted) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Fm7|Fm7|Eb7|Eb7|Db7|C7|Fm7|Fm7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root for a beat and a half, fifth on the and of 2, octave on beat 3 held to the end of the bar. It is the dotted line with the octave on beat 3. Hold the octave its full length.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Fm7|Fm7|Eb7|Eb7|Db7|C7|Fm7|Fm7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"songfather"}},{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Fm7|Fm7|Eb7|Eb7|Db7|C7|Fm7|Fm7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"songfather"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7 D7|Gmaj7 Em7|Am7 D7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"songfather"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass.qmd#bass-dotted).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass.qmd#bass-dotted) (bass line), [Pop backbeat](drums.qmd#drums-strum) (drum groove), [Ballad](drums.qmd#drums-ballad) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in bossa nova:** [Bossa nova](chords.qmd#chords-bossa) (comping rhythm), [Bossa nova](drums.qmd#drums-bossa) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the From tunes group:** [So What: the bass call](bass.qmd#bass-sowhat), [Killer Joe: two-bar vamp](bass.qmd#bass-killerjoe), [Footprints: waltz ostinato](bass.qmd#bass-footprints), [All Blues: 6/8 vamp](bass.qmd#bass-allblues), [Chameleon: chromatic pickup](bass.qmd#bass-chameleon), [Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm](bass.qmd#bass-maiden), [Take Five: 3 + 2](bass.qmd#bass-takefive).

## Footprints: waltz ostinato {#bass-footprints}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Footprints: waltz ostinato**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar figure in 3/4 (one bar of 6/4): root, fifth, octave in quarter notes, then the third above that octave held for two beats and the fifth to lead back.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Fm7|Fm7|Cm7|Cm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Footprints: waltz ostinato","opts":{"bassFeel":"footprints"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Root and fifth

Start with something simpler. The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-alt) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Fm7|Fm7|Cm7|Cm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Chord tones (learning to walk)

The chord spelled out, one note on every beat: root, 3rd, 5th, 7th, the same in every bar. When a bar has two chords, each gets its root and one more note. A step between playing roots and walking.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-arp) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Fm7|Fm7|Cm7|Cm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Footprints: waltz ostinato, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A two-bar figure in 3/4: root, fifth, octave in the first bar, then the third above the octave held for two beats and the fifth leading back down. Feel it as one long bar of six.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Fm7|Fm7|Cm7|Cm7" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Footprints: waltz ostinato","opts":{"bassFeel":"footprints"}},{"label":"Chord tones (learning to walk) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"arp"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Cm7|Fm7|Fm7|Cm7|Cm7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Footprints: waltz ostinato","opts":{"bassFeel":"footprints"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Root and fifth](bass.qmd#bass-alt), [Chord tones (learning to walk)](bass.qmd#bass-arp).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Waltz in one](chords.qmd#chords-waltz) (comping rhythm).
- **Plays with, in swing:** [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto) (comping rhythm), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the From tunes group:** [So What: the bass call](bass.qmd#bass-sowhat), [Killer Joe: two-bar vamp](bass.qmd#bass-killerjoe), [Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-songfather), [All Blues: 6/8 vamp](bass.qmd#bass-allblues), [Chameleon: chromatic pickup](bass.qmd#bass-chameleon), [Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm](bass.qmd#bass-maiden), [Take Five: 3 + 2](bass.qmd#bass-takefive).

## All Blues: 6/8 vamp {#bass-allblues}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **All Blues: 6/8 vamp**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar figure in 6/8. Each bar is a long note and two short ones: root, fifth, sixth, then seventh, sixth, fifth.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="G7|G7|G7|G7|Gm7|Gm7|G7|G7" data-tempo="60" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-meter="6/8" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"All Blues: 6/8 vamp","opts":{"bassFeel":"allblues"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Held roots (the bass voice)

Start with something simpler. The root of every chord, held until the next chord: the bass part of a four-part hymn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-held) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="G7|G7|G7|G7|Gm7|Gm7|G7|G7" data-tempo="50" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="6/8" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: 12/8 ballad

Long notes on beats 1 and 3, root then fifth, each set up by a short note on the last eighth of the beat before.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-twelve8) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="G7|G7|G7|G7|Gm7|Gm7|G7|G7" data-tempo="50" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="6/8" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"12/8 ballad","opts":{"bassFeel":"twelve8"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: All Blues: 6/8 vamp, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** 6/8: two beats of three eighths. Each bar is a long note and two short ones: root, fifth, sixth, then seventh, sixth, fifth. Rock gently on the long notes.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="G7|G7|G7|G7|Gm7|Gm7|G7|G7" data-tempo="50" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-meter="6/8" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"All Blues: 6/8 vamp","opts":{"bassFeel":"allblues"}},{"label":"12/8 ballad (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"twelve8"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 60 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="G7|G7|G7|G7|Gm7|Gm7|G7|G7" data-tempo="60" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-meter="6/8" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"All Blues: 6/8 vamp","opts":{"bassFeel":"allblues"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Held roots (the bass voice)](bass.qmd#bass-held), [12/8 ballad](bass.qmd#bass-twelve8).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [12/8 ballad](bass.qmd#bass-twelve8) (bass line).

## Chameleon: chromatic pickup {#bass-chameleon}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Chameleon: chromatic pickup**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The root on beat 1, then two eighth notes on beat 4 that climb by semitones into the next bar's root. Only the skeleton of the record's line.

It belongs in *Boogaloo* and *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the boogaloo style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="Bbm7|Eb7|Bbm7|Eb7" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chameleon: chromatic pickup","opts":{"bassFeel":"chameleon"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Held roots (the bass voice)

Start with something simpler. The root of every chord, held until the next chord: the bass part of a four-part hymn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-held) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="Bbm7|Eb7|Bbm7|Eb7" data-tempo="70" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Roots on every beat

The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-roots) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="Bbm7|Eb7|Bbm7|Eb7" data-tempo="70" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Chameleon: chromatic pickup, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The root on beat 1, then two eighths on beat 4 climbing by half steps into the next root. Leave beats 2 and 3 empty: the silence is half the groove.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="Bbm7|Eb7|Bbm7|Eb7" data-tempo="70" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chameleon: chromatic pickup","opts":{"bassFeel":"chameleon"}},{"label":"Roots on every beat (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 100 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="Bbm7|Eb7|Bbm7|Eb7" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chameleon: chromatic pickup","opts":{"bassFeel":"chameleon"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|Bb7 C7|F7|Gm7 C7" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chameleon: chromatic pickup","opts":{"bassFeel":"chameleon"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same bass line in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Straight-eighth rock**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Chameleon: chromatic pickup","opts":{"bassFeel":"chameleon"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Held roots (the bass voice)](bass.qmd#bass-held), [Roots on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-roots).
- **Plays with, in boogaloo:** [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs) (comping rhythm), [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto) (drum groove), [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) (conga part).

## Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm {#bass-maiden}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The bass plays the comping rhythm: 1, the and of 2 and 4 in the first bar, the and of 2 and 4 in the second.

It belongs in *Boogaloo* and *Bossa nova*. Here it is in the bossa nova style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus|Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm","opts":{"bassFeel":"maiden"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus|Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)

The root on beat 1, again on the and of 2 and on beat 3, the same rhythm as the kick drum. Every second bar ends with an eighth note that leads into the next chord.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-dotted) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus|Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The bass plays the same rhythm as the chords: 1, the and of 2 and 4 in the first bar (the note on 4 held over the barline), then the and of 2 and 4. Play with the piano's left hand, not against it.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus|Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm","opts":{"bassFeel":"maiden"}},{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus|Dsus|Dsus|Fsus|Fsus" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm","opts":{"bassFeel":"maiden"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7 D7|Gmaj7 Em7|Am7 D7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm","opts":{"bassFeel":"maiden"}}]'></div>

The same bass line in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

## Root and fifth {#bass-alt}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Root and fifth**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

It belongs in *Boom-chick*, *Calypso*, *Ska / reggae*, *Country train beat*, *Acoustic strum*, *Folk carol*, *Waltz (in one)*, *John Prine Fingerpicking*, *Stride piano* and *Ragtime*. Here it is in the boom-chick style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Root and fifth, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root on 1, fifth on 3, both short so the chords can be heard on 2 and 4. The fifth is one string up and two frets up from the root, or on the string below at the same fret: use whichever is closer to the next root.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}},{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3 (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 104 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

## Root and fifth on every beat {#bass-polka}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Root and fifth on every beat**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Root, fifth, root, fifth: a note on every beat, short. Now and then, mostly at the end of a four-bar phrase, the last three eighth notes of the bar run up the scale (5-6-7) into the next bar's root. In 3/4 it is root, fifth, fifth.

It belongs in *Freylekhs / polka* and *Boom-chick*. Here it is in the freylekhs / polka style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="freylekhs" data-chart="Dm|Dm|A7|Dm" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"polka"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Root and fifth

Start with something simpler. The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-alt) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="freylekhs" data-chart="Dm|Dm|A7|Dm" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Roots on every beat

The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-roots) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="freylekhs" data-chart="Dm|Dm|A7|Dm" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Root and fifth on every beat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root, fifth, root, fifth: a short note on every beat. Get it steady at a slow tempo first, then add the run: the last three eighths of a phrase's last bar step up the scale (5, 6, 7) into the next root.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="freylekhs" data-chart="Dm|Dm|A7|Dm" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"polka"}},{"label":"Roots on every beat (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 132 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="freylekhs" data-chart="Dm|Dm|A7|Dm" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"polka"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="freylekhs" data-chart="Dm Gm|A7 Dm|Gm A7|Dm" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"polka"}}]'></div>

### Step 6: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"polka"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same bass line in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Boom-chick**

## 3+3+2 (tresillo) {#bass-tresillo}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **3+3+2 (tresillo)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The root on beat 1 and on the and of 2, the fifth on beat 4: eight eighth notes grouped 3+3+2.

It belongs in *Dance pop*, *Straight-eighth rock* and *Reggaeton*. Here it is in the dance pop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)

The root on beat 1, again on the and of 2 and on beat 3, the same rhythm as the kick drum. Every second bar ends with an eighth note that leads into the next chord.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-dotted) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: 3+3+2 (tresillo), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Count eight eighth notes and play on 1, 4 and 7: ONE two three FOUR five six SEVEN eight. That is beat 1, the and of 2 and beat 4. The first two notes are the root, the last the fifth. It is the dotted line with its third note moved later.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tresillo"}},{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am F|C G|Am F|C G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tresillo"}}]'></div>
