### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Roots on every beat

The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-roots) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Say it: ONE (and) two AND three. The note on the and of 2 is the push that makes it pop music. Every second bar, the last eighth note walks into the next root from a step below or above.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}},{"label":"Roots on every beat (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same bass line in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Piano ballad**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

**Straight-eighth rock**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

**Emo / pop-punk**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="emo" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="150" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves), [Roots on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-roots).
- **Leads to:** [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass.qmd#bass-tresillo), [Motown: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-motown), [Tango (habanera)](bass.qmd#bass-tango), [Boogaloo riff](bass.qmd#bass-riff), [Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-songfather), [Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm](bass.qmd#bass-maiden): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Pop backbeat](drums.qmd#drums-strum) (drum groove), [Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-songfather) (bass line), [Ballad](drums.qmd#drums-ballad) (drum groove), [Ballad: rocking](chords.qmd#chords-ball-rock) (comping rhythm).

## Octaves (disco) {#bass-octaves}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Octaves (disco)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The root on every beat and the root an octave up on every off-beat.

It belongs in *Dance pop*. Here it is in the dance pop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Octaves (disco)","opts":{"bassFeel":"octaves"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on every beat

Start with something simpler. The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-roots) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Root eighths

The root on every eighth note, the beats a little louder: the rock bass line under With or Without You and a thousand others.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-eighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root eighths","opts":{"bassFeel":"eighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Octaves (disco), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root on the beat, the same note an octave higher on the off-beat. The octave is two strings up and two frets up: the hand stays in one place and the plucking hand jumps strings. Keep both notes short and the off-beats as loud as the beats.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Octaves (disco)","opts":{"bassFeel":"octaves"}},{"label":"Root eighths (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"eighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Octaves (disco)","opts":{"bassFeel":"octaves"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am F|C G|Am F|C G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Octaves (disco)","opts":{"bassFeel":"octaves"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-roots), [Root eighths](bass.qmd#bass-eighths).
- **Leads to:** [Boogie-woogie octaves](bass.qmd#bass-boogie-oct): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Four on the floor](drums.qmd#drums-dance) (drum groove), [Hi-hat: open off-beats](drums.qmd#drums-hhdance) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in dance pop:** [3+3+2 (tresillo)](chords.qmd#chords-tresillo) (comping rhythm), [Four on the floor](drums.qmd#drums-dance) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Roots on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-roots), [Root and fifth](bass.qmd#bass-alt), [Root and fifth on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-polka), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass.qmd#bass-tresillo), [Root eighths](bass.qmd#bass-eighths), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass.qmd#bass-dotted), [Motown: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-motown), [12/8 ballad](bass.qmd#bass-twelve8).

## Motown: root, fifth, octave {#bass-motown}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Motown: root, fifth, octave**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A two-bar line: the root on 1 and the and of 2, the fifth on 3, then the octave and fifth in eighths; the second bar ends by leading into the next chord. A plain stand-in for a Motown bass part, which would move far more.

It belongs in *Motown / soul*. Here it is in the motown / soul style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Motown: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"motown"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Root and fifth

Start with something simpler. The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-alt) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)

The root on beat 1, again on the and of 2 and on beat 3, the same rhythm as the kick drum. Every second bar ends with an eighth note that leads into the next chord.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-dotted) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Motown: root, fifth, octave, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A two-bar line. The first bar is the dotted rhythm with the fifth on beat 3, then octave and fifth in eighths. The second bar leads by step into the next chord. Play it lightly and short; a Motown bass part bounces.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Motown: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"motown"}},{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Motown: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"motown"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C Am|F G|C Am|F G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Motown: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"motown"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Root and fifth](bass.qmd#bass-alt), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass.qmd#bass-dotted).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [The Barbara Ann rhythm](chords.qmd#chords-barbara) (comping rhythm), [Motown](drums.qmd#drums-motown) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in motown / soul:** [The Barbara Ann rhythm](chords.qmd#chords-barbara) (comping rhythm), [Motown](drums.qmd#drums-motown) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Roots on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-roots), [Root and fifth](bass.qmd#bass-alt), [Root and fifth on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-polka), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass.qmd#bass-tresillo), [Root eighths](bass.qmd#bass-eighths), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass.qmd#bass-dotted), [Octaves (disco)](bass.qmd#bass-octaves), [12/8 ballad](bass.qmd#bass-twelve8).

## 12/8 ballad {#bass-twelve8}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **12/8 ballad**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Long notes on beats 1 and 3, root then fifth, each set up by a short note on the last eighth of the beat before.

It belongs in *12/8 doo-wop*. Here it is in the 12/8 doo-wop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"12/8 ballad","opts":{"bassFeel":"twelve8"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Two-feel

Half notes on beats 1 and 3, root then fifth, with an occasional pickup into the next bar. The lighter feel a band often plays on the head before the bass starts to walk.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-two) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Two-feel","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: 12/8 ballad, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Count the bar as four beats of three: ONE-and-a TWO-and-a. The long notes on 1 and 3 (root, then fifth) each have a short pickup on the last eighth before them. Let the long notes ring; keep the pickup light.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="50" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"12/8 ballad","opts":{"bassFeel":"twelve8"}},{"label":"Two-feel (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"two"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 66 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"12/8 ballad","opts":{"bassFeel":"twelve8"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="doowop" data-chart="C Am|F G|C Am|F G" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"12/8 ballad","opts":{"bassFeel":"twelve8"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves), [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two).
- **Leads to:** [All Blues: 6/8 vamp](bass.qmd#bass-allblues): the patterns that use this one as a step.

- **Plays with, in 12/8 doo-wop:** [Triplet chords (12/8)](chords.qmd#chords-triplets) (comping rhythm), [12/8](drums.qmd#drums-twelve8) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Roots on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-roots), [Root and fifth](bass.qmd#bass-alt), [Root and fifth on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-polka), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass.qmd#bass-tresillo), [Root eighths](bass.qmd#bass-eighths), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass.qmd#bass-dotted), [Octaves (disco)](bass.qmd#bass-octaves), [Motown: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-motown).

## Held roots (the bass voice) {#bass-held}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Held roots (the bass voice)**. It is one of the first patterns to learn, so this page starts from it and takes it into the band. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The root of every chord, held until the next chord: the bass part of a four-part hymn.

It belongs in *Hymn (four parts)*, *Folk carol* and *Piano ballad*. Here it is in the hymn (four parts) style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Held roots (the bass voice), slowly

**How to play it.** Pluck once, then let the note ring right through the bar: the left hand keeps the string down until the chord changes. This is the whole job of the bass in a hymn: the lowest voice, held. Listen to how each new root moves the chord above it.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="56" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 80 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C|F|G|C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="hymn" data-chart="C F|G C|Am F|G C" data-tempo="80" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same bass line in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Folk carol**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

**Piano ballad**

## Roots on 1 and 3 {#bass-halves}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Roots on 1 and 3**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

It belongs in *Folk carol*, *Hymn (four parts)*, *Piano ballad* and *Acoustic strum*. Here it is in the folk carol style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Held roots (the bass voice)

Start with something simpler. The root of every chord, held until the next chord: the bass part of a four-part hymn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-held) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Roots on 1 and 3, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Two notes a bar, both the root. Count 1-2-3-4 aloud and pluck on 1 and 3. Let each note last its full two beats; the gap before the next one should be tiny. When a bar has two chords, the second root simply arrives on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="68" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}},{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G C|D G|C D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same bass line in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Hymn (four parts)**

**Piano ballad**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

**Acoustic strum**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

- **Leads to:** [Roots on every beat](bass.qmd#bass-roots), [Root and fifth](bass.qmd#bass-alt), [Root eighths](bass.qmd#bass-eighths), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass.qmd#bass-dotted), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass.qmd#bass-tresillo), [12/8 ballad](bass.qmd#bass-twelve8), [Bossa nova](bass.qmd#bass-bossa), [Tango (habanera)](bass.qmd#bass-tango), [Cha-cha](bass.qmd#bass-chacha), [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two), [Chord tones (learning to walk)](bass.qmd#bass-arp), [Walking](bass.qmd#bass-walk), [Yancey figure](bass.qmd#bass-yancey), [Boogaloo riff](bass.qmd#bass-riff), [Killer Joe: two-bar vamp](bass.qmd#bass-killerjoe), [Song for My Father: root, fifth, octave](bass.qmd#bass-songfather), [Maiden Voyage: roots on the rhythm](bass.qmd#bass-maiden), [Take Five: 3 + 2](bass.qmd#bass-takefive): the patterns that use this one as a step.

## Bossa nova {#bass-bossa}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Bossa nova**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Root on 1 and fifth on 3, each one set up by an eighth note just before it: the fifth on the and of 2, the next chord's root on the and of 4.

It belongs in *Bossa nova*. Here it is in the bossa nova style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"bassFeel":"bossa"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Root and fifth

The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-alt) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Bossa nova, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root on 1, fifth on 3, and each one set up by an eighth note just before it: the fifth on the and of 2, and on the and of 4 the root of the next bar's chord. The low notes sound like a heartbeat: long, short-long, short.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"bassFeel":"bossa"}},{"label":"Root and fifth (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7|D7|Gmaj7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"bassFeel":"bossa"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="bossa" data-chart="Am7 D7|Gmaj7 Em7|Am7 D7|Gmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"bassFeel":"bossa"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Other bass lines in the Latin group:** [Tango (habanera)](bass.qmd#bass-tango), [Tumbao](bass.qmd#bass-tumbao), [Cha-cha](bass.qmd#bass-chacha).

## Tango (habanera) {#bass-tango}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Tango (habanera)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The habanera rhythm: root held for a beat and a half, the fifth on the and of 2, then the root an octave up on 3 and the fifth on 4.

It belongs in *Tango*. Here it is in the tango style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tango"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Roots on 1 and 3

Start with something simpler. The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-halves) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)

The root on beat 1, again on the and of 2 and on beat 3, the same rhythm as the kick drum. Every second bar ends with an eighth note that leads into the next chord.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-dotted) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Tango (habanera), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The habanera: a long root (a beat and a half), the fifth on the and of 2, then the octave on 3 and the fifth on 4. Play it marked and a little heavy, with every note clearly separated.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tango"}},{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 104 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am Dm|E7 Am|Dm E7|Am" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"bassFeel":"tango"}}]'></div>

## Tumbao {#bass-tumbao}

*For bass, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Tumbao**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The Cuban bass line that never plays beat 1: the fifth on the and of 2, then on beat 4 the root of the NEXT bar's chord, held over the barline.

It belongs in *Son montuno* and *Cha-cha*. Here it is in the son montuno style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

### Step 1: Root and fifth

Start with something simpler. The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-alt) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

Root on 1 and fifth on 3, each one set up by an eighth note just before it: the fifth on the and of 2, the next chord's root on the and of 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-bossa) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="70" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Bossa nova","opts":{"bassFeel":"bossa"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Tumbao, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Do not play on beat 1. The fifth lands on the and of 2; on beat 4 you play the root of the next bar's chord early and hold it across the barline. Count aloud and clap beat 1 while you play, so you feel where the chord changes even though you are ahead of it.

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C F|G7 C|C F|G7 C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tumbao","opts":{"bassFeel":"tumbao"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Root and fifth

The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass.qmd#bass-alt) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Cha-cha, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root held through 1 and 2, fifth on 3, root on 4: three notes that sit under the cha-cha-cha of the chords. Keep beat 3 and beat 4 short and even, like the dancers' feet.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"bassFeel":"chacha"}},{"label":"Root and fifth (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am|Dm|E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"bassFeel":"chacha"}}]'></div>

### Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="chacha" data-chart="Am Dm|E7 Am|Dm E7|Am" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Cha-cha","opts":{"bassFeel":"chacha"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves), [Root and fifth](bass.qmd#bass-alt).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Cha-cha](chords.qmd#chords-chacha) (comping rhythm), [Cha-cha](drums.qmd#drums-chacha) (drum groove), [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) (conga part).
- **Plays with, in cha-cha:** [Cha-cha](chords.qmd#chords-chacha) (comping rhythm), [Cha-cha](drums.qmd#drums-chacha) (drum groove), [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) (conga part).
- **Other bass lines in the Latin group:** [Bossa nova](bass.qmd#bass-bossa), [Tango (habanera)](bass.qmd#bass-tango), [Tumbao](bass.qmd#bass-tumbao).
